thread.title: Retail Down Despite Strong Monthly Figures

author: Nasdaq
title: Retail Down Despite Strong Monthly Figures
text:
Shutterstock photo Wednesday, August 15, 2018, 10:15 AM, EST NASDAQ Composite -1.33% Dow -1.05% S&P 500 -1.03% Russell 2000 -0.76% NASDAQ Advancers: 468 Decliners: 1469 Today's Volume (vs. yesterday) +35.8% U.S. equity markets opened in the red today and are trading broadly lower as the Dow and the S&P 500 Indexes both snapped a 4 day losing streak yesterday. Trading volumes continue to trend below yearly averages as the summer trading malaise takes grip. Tencent set the tone with a disappointing earnings report, which hurt Chinese internet stocks and tech generally. Tech of course has led the market and so weakness there hurts the broader averages. Commodities are also weaker today, which seems related to emerging markets & Turkey news but also is weighing on sentiment. 409 of the S&P 500 companies are trading lower Currently 9 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors are trading lower with Energy and Material the worst performing sectors. Crude oil and Gold both trade lower. The dollar is higher while the yield on the 10-yr has retreated to 2.8479 after yielding more that 3% to start August.
U.S. household debt continues to increase. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York released its Q2'18 report on Household Debt and Credit, which shows that total household debt increased $454 billion for the quarter to $13.3 trillion marking the 16 th consecutive quarter with an increase, breaking the previous record set in 2008. Mortgages make up the bulk of the debt, followed by student loan debt, auto loans then credit card debt. "While overall delinquency rates have remained stable at relatively low levels, transition rates into delinquency have fallen noticeably for student loan over the past year, reflecting an improved labor market and increased participation in various income-driven repayment plans," Wilbert van der Klaauw, senior vice president at the New York Fed. U.S. Retail Sales for July were strong, showing growth of 0.5% vs expectations of 0.1%. Ex-auto's was even stronger reporting 0.6% growth vs expectations of only 0.3% increase. However, June's sales were revised lower to 0.2% vs a previously reported growth of 0.5%. Retail sales have increased 6.4% over the past 12 months, close to the long-run average since 1980. Consumer spending plays a major part in the U.S. GDP, as two-thirds of U.S. economic activity is related to consumer spend. The mandatory SEC 13F quarterly holdings filings are due today. SEC Form 13F is a quarterly report that is filed by institutional investment managers (hedge funds, mutual funds, trusts, pension, insurance and investment advisors) with at least $100 million in equity assets under management (AUM) detailing their stock positions for the previous quarter. So it is a look back at the stocks they owned on the last day of the previous quarter. So one of the most widely followed filers, Warren Buffet's Berkshire Hathaway filed showed an increase in their position in Apple (AAPL), the 1 st stock with a $1 trillion market cap, by 12.3 million shares to 251.9 million shares valuing the stake at over $525 billion. Technical Take: Retail Down Despite Strong Monthly Figures
Despite strong monthly retail sales figures released earlier today, the S&P Retail ETF, ticker XRT, is down 2.5% which may be more attributable to "sell the news" and quarterly earnings amongst individual members within the index. The XRT is up 11.9% YTD, outpacing most benchmarks that are not over-weighted in technology. Just yesterday the XRT saw its highest close since June 22, a minor breakout of what looks like a large cup and handle continuation pattern forming throughout much of 2018. Despite today's weakness the XRT remains above its 50-day sma, while all its moving averages are trending higher and properly lined up. The longer term technical setup remains constructive at this time.
